# Valence: Equity Valuation & Financial Modeling Workbench

Valence is a free, browser-based equity-valuation and 3-statement financial
modeling workbench for US and Indian equities. It reads a company's own annual
filings, builds a model from them, runs its own audit before showing a number,
and exports the whole thing as a live Excel workbook.

URL: https://valence.sourabhpradhan.in/
Author: Sourabh (https://www.sourabhpradhan.in/)
Source: https://github.com/karbburn

---

## What Valence does

An analyst can value a public company end to end in the browser:

- Search any onboarded US (NASDAQ/NYSE) or Indian (NSE/BSE) ticker.
- Inspect a normalized 3-statement model (Income Statement, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow).
- Override operating drivers and recompute the model.
- Switch between Base, Bull, and Bear scenarios.
- Export a 31-tab Excel model with live formulas.
- Read the audit, check by check, including what each check tests and why.

## The reverse DCF is the distinctive part

Valence runs the valuation backwards. Given a market price it solves for the
perpetuity growth rate that price requires, in closed form. A DCF normally takes
a growth rate as an input and produces a price, which means the answer is a
consequence of the assumption rather than a statement about the market. The
reverse DCF inverts that: it takes the market's number and returns the assumption
it embeds, which is the part that can be argued with.

For a target price to be worth anything, the growth it requires has to be
defensible forever. Stating that requirement in the same units as the forecast is
what makes it arguable.

## Capabilities

### Driver-based 5-year forecasting
Projects the Income Statement, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow Statement across
Base, Bull, and Bear scenarios, driven by operating metrics: Revenue Growth,
EBITDA/EBIT Margins, CapEx % Revenue, D&A %, DSO, DPO, and Tax Rate.

### DCF and WACC build-up
Full Free Cash Flow to Firm (FCFF) build with Non-Cash Operating Working Capital
changes, mid-year discounting, dynamic WACC (CAPM cost of equity plus a
tax-shielded cost of debt), Gordon-Growth and Exit EV/EBITDA terminal values, and
an Enterprise Value to Implied Share Price bridge that names the basis of each
term.

### Trading comps, and why they are not averaged in
Peer benchmarking on EV/Sales, EV/EBITDA, P/E, FCF Yield, and ROIC, presented as a
football-field range across methods. The multiples are computed and shown, and
are deliberately kept out of the headline valuation. The methods disagree, and a
blended number hides which method produced the answer and by how much. Presenting
the disagreement is more useful than averaging it away.

### PE exit returns and IRR
3-year and 5-year prospective Exit Equity Value, MoIC, and Equity IRR under Base,
Bull, and Bear exit scenarios, with entry-price sensitivity.

### Multi-market and multi-currency
US equities (NASDAQ/NYSE, USD millions) and Indian equities (NSE/BSE, INR crores),
with currency and unit localization across all statements.

### Audit engine
The engine runs its own checks and publishes them: 4 accounting, 3 valuation, and
9 data-quality checks in total. A check whose inputs are absent reports N/A and
is never counted as a pass, because a check that did not run has not cleared
anything. The number of checks is read from the engine rather than fixed in the
description of it, so the two cannot drift.

### 31-tab interactive Excel exporter
Live .xlsx workbooks where the detail schedules drive the operating model, with
real Excel formulas rather than pasted values: CAPM, FCFF sums, cross-sheet
references, 2D sensitivity grids, and live =IF() audit checks. A reader can open
one, change a driver, and watch the model move.

## Methodology

### DCF
Unlevered FCFF discounted at WACC. Two terminal methods: Gordon Growth
(perpetuity) and an Exit EV/EBITDA multiple. Enterprise Value bridges to Equity
Value via net debt, then to an Implied Share Price on diluted shares.

### WACC
Cost of equity by the Capital Asset Pricing Model; cost of debt tax-shielded;
capital weights at market value.

### Reverse DCF
Given the market price, Valence inverts the DCF for the market-implied perpetuity
growth rate in closed form.

## How to read a figure from this site, and how to check it

Every price is dated. A ticker page states the market price, the exchange close it
is taken from, and the date of that session. A valuation compared against an
undated price cannot be checked by anyone, so the date is part of the figure
rather than a footnote to it.

A price is the close of a completed session, never a live print taken mid-session.
A model is revalued when a newer session closes, so a page does not sit on
yesterday's close because it was popular enough to stay in a cache.

Filings are read from the company's own annual reports. Where a figure could not
be sourced, the engine reports it as unavailable rather than estimating it, and a
check that could not run is marked N/A rather than passed.

## Coverage and limits

- Coverage is onboarded per ticker, so a listed company is not necessarily present.
- IFRS filers that report under ifrs-full rather than us-gaap are not yet read, and
  their tickers report as unavailable rather than being guessed at.
- Indian coverage depends on exchange and aggregator availability, which is less
  reliable than SEC EDGAR and degrades for some symbols.
- Cost of debt is an estimate where a company has no traded debt, and is labelled
  as an estimate in the workbook.
- Beta is a published benchmark figure adjusted toward one, not a regression
  computed from this site's own price history.

## FAQ

**What is DCF valuation?** It estimates a company's intrinsic value by projecting
future free cash flows and discounting them to present value at the weighted
average cost of capital.

**What is WACC?** The blended required return on a company's equity and debt,
used as the discount rate in a DCF.

**Which markets does Valence cover?** US equities (NASDAQ/NYSE, USD) and Indian
equities (NSE/BSE, INR), onboarded per ticker.

**Where does the data come from?** SEC EDGAR XBRL for US filers, exchange and
aggregator sources for India, and exchange closing prices for the benchmark.

**Is Valence free?** Yes. It is a free, browser-based workbench. Saved models live
in the browser and are not uploaded to a server.

**Can I export to Excel?** Yes. A 31-tab .xlsx with live formulas.

## Author and technology

Built by Sourabh. The engine is Python 3.12 with Pydantic v2; the API is FastAPI
and Uvicorn; the Excel renderer uses OpenPyXL; data is persisted in SQLite. The
dashboard is a Next.js application with a custom dark theme.
